name: eas-observe
description: Use for anything related to EAS Observe - adding `expo-observe` to an Expo project (AppMetricsRoot/ObserveRoot HOC, markInteractive and ObserveInteractiveMarker, the useObserve hook, the Expo Router / React Navigation integrations for per-route metrics, the expo-image and Reanimated integrations, user-defined events via `Observe.logEvent`, error reporting via ObserveErrorBoundary and `Observe.reportError`, native crash reporting, source map upload for symbolicated stack traces, and runtime config such as sampleRate and dispatchInDebug), querying via the EAS CLI (`eas observe:metrics-summary`, `observe:metrics`, `observe:routes`, `observe:events`, `observe:session`, `observe:versions`, `observe:errors`, `observe:event`) or the Expo MCP `observe_*` tools, interpreting the resulting metrics (cold/warm launch, TTR, TTI, navigation cold/warm TTR, update download, and the TTI frameRate/device/network params for triaging slow startups), or shipping an Observe integration inside a third-party package.

npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:events expo-image.oversized
npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:errors
npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:events reanimated.warning
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:metrics-summary` | Per-version statistical aggregates for startup and navigation metrics (median, p90, etc.) |
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:metrics` | Individual metric samples ordered by value or timestamp (paginated) |
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:routes` | Per-route statistical aggregates for navigation metrics (Nav Cold TTR, Nav Warm TTR, Nav TTI) |
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:events` | Custom events emitted by the app via `logEvent` — name summary, all events, or filtered by event name (paginated)
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:session` | Full timeline of metric and log events for one session |
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:versions` | App version hierarchy with build numbers, OTA update IDs, and event counts |
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:errors` | Error groups by fingerprint; `--fingerprint <id>` lists one group's occurrences with stack traces |
| `npx --yes eas-cli@latest observe:event` | One metric, log, or error event by its ID, taken from the `--json` output of `observe:session`, `observe:metrics`,
